name: Kristi Noem
role: U.S. Representative from South Dakota (2011–2019), governor of South Dakota (2019–2025), U.S. Secretary of Homeland Security (2025–2026)
summary: Republican politician whose record is conservative on abortion, guns, taxes, health care, energy and immigration. As governor she opposed COVID restrictions and marijuana legalization and backed restrictions on transgender athletes; as DHS Secretary she led an expanded deportation and self-deportation push.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Voted to repeal the Affordable Care Act and opposed Medicaid expansion in South Dakota as too costly.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Helped write the 2017 tax-cut law, cut the corporate rate to 21%, signed the Taxpayer Protection Pledge and opposes the estate tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Called the estate ('death') tax a pernicious double tax (2015).

cut-welfare.rationale: Backed Medicaid cuts in the Ryan budget, declined the federal $300 unemployment supplement (2020) and rejected federal summer-meal money as governor.

limit-guns.rationale: Signed the 2019 repeal of South Dakota's concealed-carry permit requirement; supports an individual right to bear arms and national concealed-carry reciprocity.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Opposed the 2020 legalization ballot measures and sued to overturn Amendment A; vetoed an industrial hemp bill in 2019.

abortion-legal.rationale: Co-sponsored federal abortion bans, signed restrictive laws in 2019, and the state's trigger ban after Dobbs had only a life exception, which she defended; by 2024 said law should be set by states.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Supported a constitutional amendment against same-sex marriage (2010) and signed the 2021 religious-refusal expansion. The marriage statement is dated 2010; no later change found.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Pushed to bar transgender athletes from girls' sports (2021) and supported prohibiting medical treatment for transgender minors (2023).

more-religion-public.rationale: Pushed a school-prayer bill (HB 1015, 2022) and says rights come from God.

separate-church-state.rationale: Pushed prayer in public schools (2022) and signed a religious-refusal law.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Backed a school-prayer bill, which suggests she does not favour excluding religion from state schools; instruction itself not addressed.

school-vouchers.rationale: Supported school vouchers (2015) and proposed education savings accounts as governor (2025).

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Proposed repealing the state's 4.5% tax on food sales (2022).

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Proposed a balanced budget amendment and voted for the Budget Control Act.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Proposed a balanced budget amendment to the U.S. Constitution (2011).

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Backed Keystone XL, offshore drilling and opening federal land to drilling.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Signed the No Climate Tax Pledge, doubted climate science (2022) and rejected federal money to fight climate change (2024).

reduce-immigration.rationale: As DHS Secretary ended temporary protected status for hundreds of thousands, ran self-deportation campaigns and pursued mass removals; earlier backed suspending refugee admissions.

open-borders.rationale: Called the border an existential threat; DHS enforcement policy under her opposed unauthorized presence.

empower-police-military.rationale: Supported $515B military spending (2015), tough-on-crime ratings, and expanded ICE hiring and enforcement at DHS.

military-superiority.rationale: Supported high military budgets (2015) and prevention of an Iranian nuclear weapon.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Opposed private retirement accounts and said she would not privatize Social Security (2010).

close-ties-china.rationale: Called the Chinese Communist Party the greatest external challenge and signed 2022-23 device bans on Chinese-owned apps.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Signed a 2024 law barring entities from China and five other states from buying South Dakota farmland; opposed Chinese purchases. Not an all-foreigners ban.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Called for training and equipping the Syrian opposition (2014).

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Signed S.B. 124 (2021) letting businesses cite religious belief to refuse services; general statement not stated by her.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Her sex-based sports position implies she treats sex and gender as fixed; no direct statement found.

notes: Dated positions: same-sex marriage (2010), abortion (federal ban support until 2024, then state-level). Quotes in the DHS release were from a spokesperson. Sources are secondary compilations plus one DHS release; no full texts of her book were available. Removed as DHS Secretary March 2026.
